source_text:
Οἷς ἐντυχόντες καὶ ἀκούσαντες μετὰ σπουδῆς εἴσεσθε, ὅσα παρέχει ὁ θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν ὀρθῶς, οἱ γενόμενοι παράδεισος τρυφῆς, πάγκαρπον ξύλον εὐθαλοῦν ἀνατείλαντες ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, ποικίλοις καρποῖς κεκοσμημένοι.
ἐν γὰρ τούτῳ τῷ χωρίῳ ξύλον γνώσεως καὶ ξύλον ζωῆς πεφύτευται: ἀλλ’ οὐ τὸ τῆς γνώσεως ἀναιρεῖ, ἀλλ’ ἡ παρακοὴ ἀναιρεῖ.
οὐδὲ γὰρ ἄσημα τὰ γεγραμμένα, ὡς θεὸς ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ξύλον γνώσεως καὶ ξύλον ζωῆς ἐν μέσῳ παραδείσου ἐφύτευσε, διὰ γνώσεως ζωὴν ἐπιδεικνύς: ᾗ μὴ καθαρῶς χρησάμενοι οἱ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς πλάνῃ τοῦ ὄφεως γεγύμνωνται.
οὐδὲ γὰρ ζωὴ ἄνευ γνώσεως οὐδὲ γνῶσις ἀσφαλὴς ἄνευ ζωῆς ἀληθοῦς: διὸ πλησίον ἑκάτερον πεφύτευται.
ἣν δύναμιν ἐνιδὼν ὁ ἀπόστολος τήν τε ἄνευ ἀληθείας προστάγματος εἰς ζωὴν ἀσκουμένην γνῶσιν μεμφόμενος λέγει: Ἡ γνῶσις φυσιοῖ, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη οἰκοδομεῖ.
ὁ γὰρ νομίζων εἰδέναι τι ἄνευ γνώσεως ἀληθοῦς καὶ μαρτυρουμένης ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς οὐκ ἔγνω, ὑπὸ τοῦ ὄφεως πλανᾶται, μὴ ἀγαπήσας τὸ ζῆν. ὁ δὲ μετὰ φόβου ἐπιγνοὺς καὶ ζωὴν ἐπιζητῶν ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι φυτεύει, καρπὸν προσδοκῶν.
ἤτω σοὶ καρδία γνῶσις, ζωὴ δὲ λόγος ἀληθής, χωρούμενος.
οὗ ξύλον φέρων καὶ καρπὸν αἱρῶν τρυγήσεις ἀεὶ τὰ παρὰ θεῷ ποθούμενα, ὧν ὄφις οὐχ ἅπτεται οὐδὲ πλάνη συγχρωτίζεται: οὐδὲ Εὔα φθείρεται, ἀλλὰ παρθένος πιστεύεται:
καὶ σωτήριον δείκνυται, καὶ ἀπόστολοι συνετίζονται, καὶ τὸ κυρίου πάσχα προέρχεται, καὶ καιροὶ συνάγονται καὶ μετὰ κόσμου ἁρμόζονται, καὶ διδάσκων ἁγίους ὁ λόγος εὐφραίνεται, δἰ οὗ πατὴρ δοξάζεται: ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. ἀμήν.
thought_title: The two trees and true knowledge
orientation: The author is closing his letter to Diognetus by explaining that the paradise trees of knowledge and life show that true knowledge must be joined with true life, and that the apostle's saying about knowledge and love confirms this.
pass_a_gloss: When you have encountered these things and heard them with eagerness, you will know all that God provides to those who love rightly, who have become a paradise of delight, having caused a fruit-bearing tree to spring up in themselves, flourishing, adorned with varied fruits. For in this place a tree of knowledge and a tree of life have been planted; but the tree of knowledge does not kill, but disobedience kills. For the things written are not without meaning, as God from the beginning planted a tree of knowledge and a tree of life in the middle of paradise, showing life through knowledge; which those from the beginning, not having used purely, were stripped bare by the deceit of the serpent. For neither is there life without knowledge, nor is knowledge secure without true life; therefore each has been planted near the other. Having seen this power, the apostle, faulting the knowledge that is practiced for life without the truth of the commandment, says: Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up. For the one who thinks he knows something without true knowledge and without knowledge witnessed by life has not known, is led astray by the serpent, not having loved to live. But the one who has known with fear and seeks life plants on hope, expecting fruit. Let knowledge be a heart to you, and life a true word, set apart. Bearing its tree and taking its fruit, you will always harvest the things desired with God, which the serpent does not touch and deceit does not come near; nor is Eve corrupted, but a virgin is believed; and salvation is shown, and apostles are made wise, and the Lord's Passover comes forth, and seasons are gathered and fitted together with the world, and the Word, teaching the saints, rejoices, through whom the Father is glorified; to whom be the glory forever. Amen.

choices.why: The phrase echoes the Septuagint's 'paradise of delight' (Genesis 2:15), and 'delight' preserves the concrete sense of τρυφή as luxurious pleasure rather than a more abstract 'luxury' or 'pleasure-garden.'

choices.term: πάγκαρπον ξύλον εὐθαλοῦν ἀνατείλαντες ἐν ἑαυτοῖς
choices.english: having caused a fruit-bearing tree to spring up in themselves, flourishing
choices.why: The participle ἀνατείλαντες is active: the lovers of God cause the tree to spring up within themselves. 'Fruit-bearing' for πάγκαρπον keeps the all-fruit sense without the awkward 'all-fruited,' and 'flourishing' for εὐθαλοῦν keeps the botanical image.

choices.term: ἀλλ’ οὐ τὸ τῆς γνώσεως ἀναιρεῖ, ἀλλ’ ἡ παρακοὴ ἀναιρεῖ
choices.english: but the tree of knowledge does not kill, but disobedience kills
choices.why: The repetition of ἀναιρεῖ is emphatic and must be kept. 'Kill' is the literal sense of ἀναιρέω here, and the contrast between the tree and disobedience is the point: the tree itself is not deadly.
The dative ᾗ is instrumental with χρησάμενοι ('using which'), and καθαρῶς means 'purely' in a moral sense. The participle is causal: because they did not use it purely, they were stripped bare.
rejected: which they did not use cleanly
not having made pure use of it

choices.why: The perfect passive of γυμνόω alludes to the nakedness of Adam and Eve after the fall in Genesis 3:7. 'Stripped bare' captures both the literal nakedness and the sense of being exposed and deprived.

choices.term: ἤτω σοὶ καρδία γνῶσις, ζωὴ δὲ λόγος ἀληθής, χωρούμενος
choices.english: Let knowledge be a heart to you, and life a true word, received
choices.why: The imperative ἤτω governs both clauses. 'A heart to you' keeps the dative of possession and the startling metaphor: knowledge becomes the reader's heart. χωρούμενος is a passive participle modifying λόγος: the true word is received or taken in.
rejected: and life be a true word

bible_refs.note: ξύλον γνώσεως καὶ ξύλον ζωῆς ἐν μέσῳ παραδείσου ἐφύτευσε
Ἡ γνῶσις φυσιοῖ, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη οἰκοδομεῖ

pass_b_english: When you encounter these things and hear them with eagerness, you will know all that God provides to those who love him rightly. They become a paradise of delight, causing a fruit-bearing tree to spring up within themselves, flourishing and adorned with many kinds of fruit.
For in this place a tree of knowledge and a tree of life have been planted. But the tree of knowledge does not kill; disobedience kills.

For what is written is not without meaning: God from the beginning planted a tree of knowledge and a tree of life in the middle of the paradise, showing life through knowledge. But those from the beginning did not use it purely, and through the deceit of the serpent they were stripped bare.
For there is no life without knowledge, and no secure knowledge without true life. That is why each tree was planted near the other.
The apostle saw this power at work, and when he criticized knowledge practiced for life without the truth of the commandment, he says: “Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up” (1 Corinthians 8:1).

For the one who thinks he knows something without true knowledge that is witnessed by life has not known; he is deceived by the serpent, because he did not love to live. But the one who knows with fear and seeks life plants in hope, expecting fruit.
Let knowledge be your heart, and life the true Word, set apart.

If you carry the wood of this tree and pick its fruit, you will always harvest what is longed for in God’s presence, things the serpent does not touch and deceit does not come near. Eve is not corrupted, but is believed as a virgin.

And salvation is shown, and the apostles are given understanding, and the Lord’s Passover goes forth, and the seasons are gathered together and joined with the world, and the Word teaches the saints and rejoices, through whom the Father is glorified. To him be glory forever. Amen.

problems.quote: you will know all that God gives to those who love him rightly
problems.source_quote: εἴσεσθε, ὅσα παρέχει ὁ θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν ὀρθῶς
problems.why: Greek says ‘you will enter into’ what God provides, not ‘you will know’ it.
problems.fix: you will enter into that which God provides to those who love him rightly
problems.ruling: εἴσεσθε is from εἰσέρχομαι ('enter into'), not 'know'; translator confused it with ἐπίστασθε/γνώσεσθε.

edits.old: you will know all that God gives to those who love him rightly
edits.new: you will enter into that which God provides to those who love him rightly

problems.quote: you will enter into that which God provides to those who love him rightly. They become a paradise of delight
problems.source_quote: εἴσεσθε, ὅσα παρέχει ὁ θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν ὀρθῶς, οἱ γενόμενοι παράδεισος τρυφῆς
problems.why: Subject shifts from 'you' to 'they'; οἱ ἀγαπῶσιν are the ones who become paradise, not a separate 'they'.
problems.fix: you will know how much God provides to those who love him rightly, having become a paradise of delight
problems.ruling: Greek uses appositive participle “οἱ γενόμενοι παράδεισος τρυφῆς” referring to “τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν ὀρθῶς”; English splits into separate sentence, shifting subject.

edits.old: you will enter into that which God provides to those who love him rightly. They become a paradise of delight
edits.new: you will know all that God provides to those who love him rightly, who become a paradise of delight

problems.quote: Let knowledge be a heart to you, and life a true word, received.
problems.source_quote: ἤτω σοὶ καρδία γνῶσις, ζωὴ δὲ λόγος ἀληθής, χωρούμενος.
problems.fix: Let knowledge be your heart, and life the true Word, set apart.
problems.ruling: χωρούμενος means 'set apart/separated'; 'received' mistranslates, changing the meaning of the clause.

edits.old: Let knowledge be a heart to you, and life a true word, received.
edits.new: Let knowledge be your heart, and life the true Word, set apart.

fixed: The mistranslation of χωρούμενος as 'received' has been corrected to 'set apart' in both the English and the literal gloss.

last_rejected.quote: But the tree of knowledge does not kill; disobedience kills.
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλ' οὐ τὸ τῆς γνώσεως ἀναιρεῖ, ἀλλ' ἡ παρακοὴ ἀναιρεῖ
last_rejected.why: ἀναιρεῖ means 'destroys' or 'abolishes', not 'kills'. The contrast is about destruction, not killing.
last_rejected.fix: But the tree of knowledge does not destroy; disobedience destroys.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀναιρεῖ can mean 'kill' in life context; translation captures meaning.

last_rejected.quote: For what is written is not without meaning
last_rejected.why: ἄσημα means 'without sign' or 'meaningless', but the sentence continues with ὡς introducing what God did; the point is that Scripture is not pointless.
last_rejected.fix: For what is written is not without significance

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by separating the description of those who love God into its own sentence, so readers can follow who becomes a paradise of delight. Kept every claim and reference intact.

notes.quote: what God (the Father) they have trusted
notes.why: Same deity called by three different titles, confusing readers.
notes.fix: Standardise to one term (e.g., “God the Father”) throughout.

notes.quote: Eve is not corrupted, but is believed as a virgin.
notes.why: The sentence is incoherent and seems a mistranslation of the Genesis account.
notes.fix: Render as “Eve remained uncorrupted and is regarded as a virgin of the new creation.”
